medium-switch.title: medium-switch
medium-switch.detail: click on the next file of the 120-file desk, every number measured from the click (not from a cold load) - the latency a reviewer actually feels

milestones.label: Baseline (audit)
milestones.note: 4 overlapping pool boots (12-16 workers, 4 copies of a 2.5 MB grammar bundle), tail-first window plan, duplicate window dispatch. Measured: medium first colour 1391 ms, worker.js 2566 KB.

milestones.label: Fixes A-F
milestones.note: One idempotent boot, one grammar attach per worker, viewport-first band split across the pool, lazy per-language grammar chunks. Measured: medium first colour 1391 -> 804-911 ms (three samples), worker.js 2566 -> 539 KB, pool:languages:load 308 -> 76 ms (the resolve moved into the boot window). The band was dispatchable at 366 ms but the first window only left at 668: the dispatch continuation was a microtask queued behind the 314 ms paint task, which fix G removes.

milestones.label: Fix G
milestones.note: Synchronous language handoff: a job whose grammars already resolved dispatches its first window in the same turn, inside the renderer's paint task instead of after it. Measured: first window sent 668 -> 344 ms, medium first colour 772 ms (against 804-911 ms with fixes A-F alone); the band finishes at 744 ms and the publish waits for the main thread to free at ~694 ms.

milestones.label: Parallelization pass
milestones.note: Job priority by attachment (window-dispatch ranks attached jobs first), pool width from hardwareConcurrency capped by the memory budget. Measured: the 5th worker cuts the 16k-line fixture's token phase 1614 -> 1275 ms (-21%) while a normal file stays inside run-to-run noise (medium first colour 713 vs 680 ms, final 1283 vs 1241); the suspected serial sections are all free (merge, publish and the open-diff clone 0-3 ms), so nothing moved to the workers.

milestones.label: Batch 1: idle warm-up, parallel boot, empty-sweep filter
milestones.note: Idle warm-up (the pool boot starts on the first idle slot), parallel boot (the highlighter and the themes resolve together), and an empty-sweep filter (sweep slots that reach no hunk are dropped). Measured: the warm-up saves 15-20 ms of boot and is a structural win only where the contents fetch is the long pole (its earlier placement is recorded as a rejected run), the parallel boot saves 15-25 ms, and the filter removes 22 of 149 windows on the 16k-line fixture (-15%); medium first colour 684 ms, bigfile 2301 ms.

milestones.label: Switch: no dispatch for a file the reviewer has left
milestones.note: Dispatch and warming both follow the reviewer. window-dispatch gives slots only to jobs with a renderer attached (a job is a snapshot; detaching and re-attaching around @pierre's converge pass only delays its own next window by one pass), and the render pass warms the NEXT file's viewport band while the pool is idle - through a side-effect-free metadata builder (diff-metadata.ts, whose parse memo the click then adopts), an off-thread parse (parse-offload.ts) and a cap of one band per warm job. Measured on the 8000-line fixture, switching to a 200-line file mid-job: before, 29 more windows of the abandoned file were dispatched (26392 ms of worker tokenize, 25 publishes) behind the reviewer's back; after, 0 new windows and only the 6 already in flight land (5275 ms). On the quiet medium desk the scoping alone leaves the reviewer's numbers unchanged (470/478 ms click->first colour against 449/477 before) - it removes contention, it does not make a quiet pool faster - while the prefetch is what shortens that wait: 375/360 ms click->first colour on the prefetched next file with 0 windows left to send at the click, against 519 ms for the same build's cold control.

rejected.label: Fix H: prime each worker's grammar with a one-line tokenize
rejected.measurement: a one-line tokenize absorbs the fixed cost (81 ms of compile, then 0.79 ms/row in Node), but compile + rows is the same worker time either way; with fix G the gate is the renderer's 359 ms paint task and the ~165 ms of clone/contention per first window, so priming is shadowed. Not landed.

targets.label: shorten the renderer's first paint task
targets.detail: 359 ms main-thread task starting right after the plain grid is handed over; our own spans inside it (render:acquire 1 ms, render:paint 10 ms) say it is the renderer's own row layout

targets.label: cut the clone/contention overhead of a first window
targets.detail: band windows: 400 ms wall for 235 ms of reported tokenize - structured-clone deserialization plus 4 workers competing with the painting main thread

targets.label: move grammar registration off the main thread
targets.detail: pool:languages:load is still 101-384 ms of chunk parse + shiki registration on the main thread. The grammar shards shrank the chunk (worker.js 2566 -> 539 KB) but registration stayed there, and letting workers import their own grammar chunk is closed by design (scripts/build-ui.mjs stubs every grammar module out of the worker build), so this needs a shape of its own - a grammar registered once and shared, or registration inside a worker.

knownWins.label: viewport-only incremental sweep (the VS Code model)
knownWins.detail: bigfile tokenizes 2154 rows across 148 windows; 88 of them contain zero changed rows. The empty-sweep filter (milestone warm) already drops those slots; what remains is a scroll-driven sweep instead of a whole-file one

knownWins.label: oniguruma wasm engine
knownWins.detail: ~1.6x faster per row (0.57 vs 0.90 ms/row measured in Node) for ~+600 KB of worker bundle; affects whole-file finalization, not first color

knownWins.label: band-sized pool
knownWins.detail: the pool is sized from the machine (hardwareConcurrency capped at 6, milestone parallel), not from the job: 4-6 workers for a 400-line first file is more parallelism than the visible band needs

knownWins.label: desk-side diff build for oversized files
knownWins.detail: the desk needs ~49.5 s to build the diff of a 2.8 MB file server-side, before the UI sees anything (separate from the token pipeline)

runs.note: grammar prewarm moved the whole resolve into the boot window: pool:languages:load 308 -> 76 ms

longTasks.label: renderer row layout after the plain grid

runs.note: dispatch moved into the paint task (668 -> 344 ms); the band now finishes at 744 and the publish waits for the main thread to free at ~694

contents: the desk needs ~49.5 s to build the diff of a 2.8 MB file server-side; the UI colors the visible rows 232 ms after the file lands NOT REPRODUCIBLE as of fix G: a fresh cold open of the same file behind the guard measures contents 34 ms, plainPaint 2725 ms, first colour 2885 ms, final 4072 ms (see bigfile-guard-cold). Treat this point as suspect: the 49.5 s was recorded in one harness run and no longer repeats; the harness also records contents as a fetch duration while the other stages are timestamps.

body-to-first-colour of the 2.8 MB / 16k-line file: the oversized-file guard was dismissed at t=2627 ms, /api/file-contents then took 34 ms for 5.98 MB, plain rows painted at 2725 ms, first colour at 2885 ms, whole file tokenized at 4072 ms (148 windows, 88 sweep + 60 cluster, 2154 rows, 4293 ms of worker tokenize in ~1.2 s wall clock = 3.6x on 4 workers, every window sent = done). contents is a fetch DURATION here (the harness records it that way); the other stages are ms from navigation start.

Before-point for the pool-size A/B (the guard was dismissed at t=1650). contents is the /api/file-contents fetch duration (37 ms, 5.98 MB); every other stage is ms from navigation start. Token phase (firstWindowSent -> final) 1614 ms; first-colour latency 87 ms; 148 windows, 2154 rows, 4258 ms of worker tokenize. Main-thread spans: pool:plain 43 ms for the whole 16k-line grid, pool:open-diff 4 posts x 2-3 ms = 9 ms, pool:merge 148 x 0 ms, pool:publish 60 x 0 ms, pool:publish:final 0 ms. Long tasks during the open: 3, 224 ms total, max 118 ms.

121-file fixture, first file auto-opened, pool at the historical 4. Token phase 914 ms; first-colour latency (firstWindowSent -> firstColor) 353 ms; 7 windows, 1000 rows. Main-thread spans: pool:plain 7 ms, pool:open-diff 4 x 0 ms, pool:merge 7 x 0 ms, pool:publish 2 x 0 ms, pool:publish:final 0 ms.

Same flow with the pool sized from hardwareConcurrency (6 cores -> 5). Token phase 1275 ms vs 1614 ms at 4 workers (-21%, -339 ms) on the same 148-window job; first-colour latency 101 ms (vs 87). 149 windows (the viewport band splits into one more chunk), 4373 ms of worker tokenize. pool:plain 45 ms. Long-task census not armed in this run.

Same flow with 5 workers (re-run after a contended first attempt whose boot took 465 ms): boot 131 ms, token phase 939 ms vs 914 ms at 4 workers, first-colour latency 369 ms vs 353 ms. A short job gains nothing from a wider pool; the extra worker costs one more grammar compile. 8 windows, 2044 ms of worker tokenize.

Batch 1 (A+B+C) with the idle warm-up placed after the settings/state fetch. Two samples of this final build: this one (boot 173 -> 291 ms, first colour 684, final 1221) and a contended one (boot 183 -> 659 ms, first colour 841, final 1444) - the pre-batch rows show the same 131-vs-465 ms boot spread, so treat the pair as the range. Recorded parallel-pool5-medium is 713/1283 and the audit run 689/1254: first colour and final stay inside the spread, and the boot is now warm before the first render pass (173 ms vs 198-205) although it still ends ~90 ms after the paint, which is why first colour does not move. What B does show consistently is the boot's own duration: highlighter || themes, 108-118 ms against 127. No `contents` stage: this route reads stage marks, not the per-request fetch timings the browser-bench rows carry.

REJECTED placement, measured twice (825/1404 and 813/1398): the warm-up scheduled before the settings/state fetch does start the boot in the fetch gap (66 ms, done at 177 - a full second before it is needed on a big file), but the highlighter engine work and the 5 worker boots then run inside the parse: painted slips 203 -> 510 ms, and first colour lands 120-140 ms later than the accepted placement. The revert is in main.ts with this measurement in its comment.

Batch 1 (A+B+C), 16k-line fixture loaded through the guard card. C is the visible change: 127 windows instead of 149 (-15%, the 22 empty sweep slots that reached no hunk). The whole pool boot is off the critical path (130 -> 177 ms, ~2 s before the first window needs a token). First colour and final sit inside the recorded spread: audit run 2077/3126 in a session whose contents fetch was 203 ms faster, recorded parallel-pool5-bigfile 4174/5348 in a session whose own note admits contention. No `contents` stage on this route. Long-task census not armed here.

Same-build cold control, click on module-core-15.ts (deliberately NOT the prefetched next file: the prefetch only warms the immediately following row). 7 windows dispatched from the click, first colour after 304 ms of worker tokenization - which is exactly the wait Fix 3b removes; the 145-160 ms gap to the warm rows is the saving a reviewer feels.

Fix 3b, click on module-core-102.ts - the file the render pass before it had PREFETCHED. firstColor = mount on purpose: the warm job's whole plan (3 windows) had already been merged before the click (pool:publish 3/3 for that job's key, pre-click), so the click sent 0 windows and the renderer took the finished grid inside its own paint. Measured from the click, same desk/session as the cold control below; the pre-Fix-3b baseline series is 449-478 ms (switch-medium-before-*/after-*) with 7 windows and 52-324 ms of tokenize before the first colour.

Fix 3b second sample, click on module-core-111.ts (prefetched by the pass that rendered the previous file). Same shape as sample 1: 0 windows sent for the clicked file, 3 sends after the click all belonging to the FOLLOWING file's prefetch job (perf marks carry the job key since this build, which is what made the attribution unambiguous).
